title: Minimum Number of Coins to be Added
summary: Given an array of coin values and a target, determine the least number of coins to add so that every integer from 1 to the target can be formed by a subsequence of the coins.
statement: Given an array of coin values and a target, determine the least number of coins to add so that every integer from 1 to the target can be formed by a subsequence of the coins. A subsequence is formed by removing some elements from the original array without changing the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: coins is nonempty, all values are positive, and target is positive.
Each coin may be selected at most once; added coins may have any positive value.
Return the fewest additions needed so every sum from one through target is obtainable.
hints: If all sums below reach are possible, only a coin no larger than reach can extend coverage without a gap.
Sort coins; consume any usable coin, otherwise add a coin worth exactly reach.
Maintain the first unreachable sum; consuming value v advances it by v, while adding reach doubles it.
A value above reach cannot form reach, so adding reach is forced-optimal at every gap and maximally extends the invariant interval.
editorial: A value above reach cannot form reach, so adding reach is forced-optimal at every gap and maximally extends the invariant interval.

tests.explanation: Adding values two and eight gives complete coverage through nineteen, and one addition cannot bridge both gaps.
The existing coins cover through three; adding four, eight, and sixteen extends coverage through twenty.
